page: Microsoft Azure D64alds_v6 is a dedicated virtual machine instance belonging to the Daldv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor with 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 2.0 threads per core, 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is bundled with 3780 GB of local disk capacity, and the instance is premium storage capable. No GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark results indicate strong overall performance, particularly in multi-threaded compute tasks. The instance achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 22158.0, placing it in the top 10% tier. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reached 391.6 GB/sec, and stress-ng multi-core CPU performance scored 98458.65, both ranking in the top 25%. Single-core performance is also strong, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2097.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 3079.97. Memory bandwidth tests show a strong cached read-only small block speed of 4863.19 GB/sec and a write large block speed of 103.51 GB/sec, though uncached large block read-only bandwidth is average at 151.26 GB/sec. For specialized tasks, the server demonstrates top-tier prompt processing speeds of 3962.73 tokens/sec for small LLM models, alongside strong performance in software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D64alds_v6 offers high compute density and substantial local storage capacity relative to its memory allocation. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio represents a tradeoff, making the instance highly efficient for compute-bound workloads but less suitable for memory-intensive applications that require larger RAM footprints per core. The integration of 3780 GB of local storage and premium storage capability supports high-throughput data operations, as evidenced by strong Passmark database operations and Redis SET performance of 88.46 million operations per second. This hardware profile is well-suited for multi-threaded processing, software compilation, static web serving, database hosting, and lightweight LLM inference tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure D64alds_v6 is a dedicated x86_64 virtual machine from the Daldv6 family, powered by a 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. It features 64 vCPUs, 128.0 GB of RAM, and 3780 GB of local storage. With a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core, this instance is optimized for compute-heavy tasks. Benchmark data highlights top-tier multi-core performance, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 22158.0 and strong multi-threaded decompression and software compilation capabilities. It also delivers strong database performance, with 88.46 million Redis SET operations per second. The lack of a GPU and the lower memory ratio are key tradeoffs, but the substantial local storage and high compute density make it highly cost-efficient for multi-threaded processing, database operations, static web serving, and lightweight LLM inference.
